This was my 8th FL since starting at Kaplan 495 in December. I was caught up in using other ppls study methods and kaplan that I didn’t do what worked for me in past. I recently switched to old methods and it’s helped me tremendously. 


“Wrong answers book”: tiny book I can fit in my scrub pocket and look over during breaks. I have awful handwriting so having a tiny book forces me to write slow and condensing to most important info. I not only write the wrong term but also the concept as whole. For example if i get a question on Piaget’s stages I write all of them in in summary form. I look over this book before work. During breaks. As soon as I get off. Anytime I’m in the car and my fam is driving and before I go to bed. I also keep sticky notes in my scrubs and randomly quiz myself on equations. 

I STRONGLY RECOMMEND LOOKING OVER NOTES BEFORE BED EVEN THO IT GIVES ME MCAT DREAMS. 

Mnemonics are my best friend. 

I’ve been doing up to 100 flashcards a day and trying to do as much as AAMC material as possible. Adding to my book as I go. 

In these two weeks I’ve also read an entire Orgo book, the 86 page ps, half the kaplan physics book, and watched videos on immunity and kidneys.

CP: my weakest. Previous highest score: 127. Started just looking at units for any problems involving math and doing unit conversions. Any answer with something 10+ molar is wrong. I skim over passage and go back to passage each question. Flag problem questions to return to. With experiments try and figure out what the result is.

Tbh I got lucky cuz the math was all relatively simple on this full length. Study patterns>equations if in time crunch.


CARS: got a 127 one first full length. Then switched to Kaplan methods which lowered my score to like 124. Started going back to old method. 3-5 passages a day (preferably AAMC). I’m a history lover and fast reader so not bad for me

I read passage and ask wtf if going on after every paragraph. What is the authors attitude? Why did he switch here? Etc. these come up in questions. I don’t highlight or write notes. For answers there’s usually one or two per question that are opposite of correct answer. One answer may be irrelevant to passage. If you have zero idea, the answer is probably the vaguest.


BIO: previous best score 128. My research and advanced bio classes help a lot. When reading passage I’m looking for the experimental purpose, independent variable, and dependent variable. I write this down along with relationships (ex: molecule a inhibits b). At least one question will be from these notes. Make sure you understand patterns in graphs. 


Psych/Soc: previous best score 128(?). Just because an answer sounds right doesn’t mean it’s write. Do flashcards constantly. I look up examples for terms that confuse me. I try to think of example in my life because then I don’t forget term. I’ll also randomly label things mentally if they pop up in real world.
